parts.article:
Sweet Trouble
 
Problems in the Australian sugar industry
 
(A) The Australian town of Mossman in the state of Queensland sits in a tropical landscape between the rainforest and the Great Barrier Reef. Eco-tourism is important there; more than 80 per cent of Douglas Shire, of which Mossman is the administrative centre, is protected by World Heritage listing. But for most of the town’s history, forest and reef have been largely irrelevant: since the sugar mill was built in 1894, the town has relied on sugarcane. Now Mossman is holding its breath. For two years the mill used by all the farms has been close to bankruptcy. It is at the centre of the economic shocks that have shaken Australia’s sugar industry, and for lifetime farmers and a long list of cane-industry workers a way of life will disappear if the mill closes. Mossman has roughly 160 growers, who now produce less than one million tonnes of the nation’s annual cane harvest of 30–40 million tonnes. But it is a microcosm of the industry. All across Australia, the cane-growing business is being squeezed between the pincers of economics and the environment.
 
(B) The ten-year average return to sugar growers throughout the 1990s was about $350 a tonne. In early 2004, sugar prices plummeted, resulting in a 25-year-low average price for Australian sugar of about $232 a tonne. Although figures vary widely across farms and regions, that was about what it cost to grow a tonne of sugar in Australia. To forestall social and economic disaster, the Government offered more than $400 million to encourage growers to leave the industry. By the end of the year, 21 farmers had taken up the offer to leave, but another 1 000 are thought to be seriously considering it, allowing those remaining to buy the vacated land and improve their economies of scale.
 
(C) Fourth-generation Mossman grower Bill Phillips-Turner is one who plans to fight on. ‘The consequences of losing the mill would be catastrophic,’ Bill says. ‘Sugar has a big economic multiplier effect: for every dollar generated from sugar, an additional $7 is generated in the wider community. Because of limited options around here, most people now employed by the industry would have to leave the area to find work.’ The farmer shareholders have so far saved the mill by accepting substantial cuts to cane payments, but this has come at a big cost to everyone. As chairman of the board of the mill, Bill has presided over some tough and unpopular decisions; the hardest was slashing the mill workforce. Assets were sold and maintenance costs cut. The board has also worked hard to find new ways of doing business. Ethanol production, where sugar is used to produce fuel, has potential, and co-generation, using cane waste to generate electric power, is another possibility. However, the most radical—but preferred—alternative is to create a future for the mill as a food factory, turning out quality sugar-based foods.
 
(D) In addition to the economic struggle, there is the environmental one. The sugar industry has the reputation of being environmentally damaging, but it has some surprising supporters. Douglas Shire mayor, Mike Berwick, is a well-known environmentalist and might be expected to be anti-cane. ‘There’s no question of the past damage it’s done to the reef through chemical and nutrient run-off*,’ he says. ‘But there’s a formula for sustainable cane production and Mossman has nearly reached it.’ Another surprise endorsement for cane comes from the Queensland Environmental Protection Agency’s sugar liaison officer, Karen Benn. ‘I’m less worried about the effect of cane on the environment than I am about other agriculture,’ she says. ‘There are good growers everywhere, but at Mossman they seem to have taken up the challenges faster.’ For example, sediment run-off, previously one of the main environmental problems caused by cane growing, is now nothing like it once was, according to Dr Brian Roberts, co-ordinator of the Douglas Shire Water Quality Improvement Program. ‘North Queensland used to hold the record for soil loss,’ he says. ‘Now … cane country is accumulating soil.’
 
(E) However, these improvements have been achieved at a great cost to growers. Now in his 60s, Tom Watters has spent a lifetime on the same farm. Fourteen years ago, he was alerted to the effect his cane could be having on Mackay Creek, the narrow waterway that receives all his run-off, and so Tom planted a 5 000-tree buffer along the edge of the creek, built up the edges of the creek with rocks to prevent erosion, and began exploring farming methods that cause minimal soil disturbance. However, none of these costly initiatives has helped him get better cane prices. Another cane grower, Doug Crees, comments that ‘Economically, it [cane growing] doesn’t make much sense. But there’s more to life than money.’ It’s this addiction to the way of life that keeps many cane farmers growing an underperforming crop. ‘It’s a good lifestyle,’ Doug says. ‘I spend eight months working on the farm and four months looking after our kids while my wife works in town. I’ve been looking at alternative crops, like forestry and cocoa, and it turns out that working away from the farm is the best diversification we could do. However, I still don’t want to do that.’
 
(F) It is difficult to see how anyone can deal satisfactorily with the passing of a way of life. Cane farmers have been part of eastern Queensland for more than a century, but despite the efforts they have put into fighting the good environmental fight, there is no guarantee that the new way of life evolving there will include cane.

groups.contentHtml:
1 Mossman cane-farming practices are close to an environmentally friendly model
2 Financial return is not the only important factor for cane growers
3 Cane sugar may not harm the environment as much as other crops do
4 The local population would decline if the sugar-processing plant closed

questions.question: Mossman cane-farming practices are close to an environmentally friendly model

analyses.content: 这里的 “sustainable”（可持续）就是题干中 “environmentally friendly model”（环境友好模式）的同义替换。
(第4段) 'But there's a formula for sustainable cane production and Mossman has nearly reached it.'
Mike Berwick 明确表示莫斯曼（Mossman）的甘蔗生产已经“几乎达到了”可持续发展的标准。

questions.question: Financial return is not the only important factor for cane growers

analyses.content: Doug 直言种甘蔗在经济上没意义，但他更看重“生活方式”，这说明钱不是唯一的因素。
你可能看到 Tom Watters 也提到了经济问题，但明确表达“生活比钱更重要”（more to life than money）的是 Doug。

(第7段) Another cane grower, Doug Crees, comments that 'Economically, it [cane growing] doesn't make much sense. But there's more to life than money.' It's this addiction to the way of life that keeps many cane farmers growing an underperforming crop.

questions.question: Cane sugar may not harm the environment as much as other crops do

analyses.content: Karen 比较了甘蔗和其他农业，表示她更担心其他农作物对环境的影响，暗示甘蔗危害较小。
题干是一个比较级（not as much as other crops），原文中的 “less worried about... than... other agriculture” 正是这种比较关系的体现。
(第4段) 'I'm less worried about the effect of cane on the environment than I am about other agriculture,' she says.

questions.question: The local population would decline if the sugar-processing plant closed

analyses.content: Bill 指出如果糖厂倒闭，由于当地就业机会有限，大多数从业者将被迫“离开该地区”去找工作，导致人口减少。
“Leave the area”（离开该地区）就是题干中 “population would decline”（人口下降）的具体表现。

(第3段) 'The consequences of losing the mill would be catastrophic, Bill says... Because of limited options around here, most people now employed by the industry would have to leave the area to find work.'

options.option: most of its people have left the town.
options.optionContent: most of its people have left the town.

options.option: a key processing plant may shut down.
options.optionContent: a key processing plant may shut down.

questions.question: In the first paragraph, the writer says that the town is ‘holding its breath’ because

analyses.content: 文中说镇子“屏住呼吸”（紧张），是因为唯一的糖厂（mill）连续两年濒临破产，面临关闭的风险。
这一段虽然提到了 B 选项的旅游业（Eco-tourism），但那只是背景介绍，让镇子紧张的核心原因是糖厂危机。
(第1段) Now Mossman is holding its breath. For two years the mill used by all the farms has been close to bankruptcy.

options.option: sell their land at a low price.
options.optionContent: sell their land at a low price.

questions.question: According to the writer, cane growers who refuse the Government offer are expected to

analyses.content: (第2段) ...allowing those remaining to buy the vacated land and improve their economies of scale.
文中提到留下的农民可以买下离开者的土地，从而改善“规模经济”，也就是扩大农场规模。
这里的 “economies of scale” 指的就是通过扩大规模来降低成本，即 A 选项的 expand。

options.option: cut the number of mill staff.
options.optionContent: cut the number of mill staff.

questions.question: Which of the following did Bill Phillips-Turner find most difficult to do?

analyses.content: 文中明确用最高级 “the hardest”（最难的）形容了裁减员工（slashing the mill workforce）这一决定。
你可能在文中也看到了出售资产（sold assets）和削减维护费（maintenance costs cut），但作者并没有说这些是“最难的”。
(第3段) As chairman of the board of the mill, Bill has presided over some tough and unpopular decisions; the hardest was slashing the mill workforce.

options.option: wants to remain on his farm.
options.optionContent: wants to remain on his farm.

options.option: wants his family to live together.
options.optionContent: wants his family to live together.

options.option: will look for part-time work in town.
options.optionContent: will look for part-time work in town.

questions.question: Cane grower Doug Crees says that he

analyses.content: Doug 虽然知道去别处工作是最好的选择，但他紧接着说“但我仍然不想那样做”，意指他想留在农场。
他确实考虑过 A 选项的替代作物（cocoa），但结论是他不想离开农场去别处工作。
(第7段) '...working away from the farm is the best diversification we could do. However, I still don't want to do that.'

questions.question: In 2004, the cost of producing sugar in Australia was similar to the selling price.

analyses.content: 文中提到2004年糖价跌至每吨232美元，而这大约就是种植一吨糖的成本，两者相当。
(第2段) In early 2004, sugar prices plummeted, resulting in a 25-year-low average price for Australian sugar of about $232 a tonne... that was about what it cost to grow a tonne of sugar in Australia.

questions.question: Farmers who accepted the Government offer have mostly moved to the city.

analyses.content: 文中只提到了有21位农民接受报价离开该行业，但完全没有提及他们搬去了哪里（比如是否去了城市）。
(第2段) By the end of the year, 21 farmers had taken up the offer to leave, but another 1 000 are thought to be seriously considering it...

questions.question: Fuel production is regarded as the most desirable alternative business for the sugar mill.

analyses.content: 文中虽然提到燃料（ethanol）有潜力，但明确指出“首选的”（preferred）替代方案是把工厂变成食品厂（food factory）。
看到 "Ethanol production" 不要急着选 True，要注意后面的转折词 "However" 引出了真正的首选方案。
(第3段) Ethanol production... has potential... However, the most radical-but preferred-alternative is to create a future for the mill as a food factory, turning out quality sugar-based foods.

questions.question: Tom Watters reduced his use of pesticides.

analyses.content: 文中列举了 Tom 做的很多环保措施（种树、堆石头防侵蚀、减少土壤扰动），但唯独没有提到减少“杀虫剂/农药”（pesticides）的使用。

(第6段) ...so Tom planted a 5 000-tree buffer along the edge of the creek, built up the edges of the creek with rocks to prevent erosion, and began exploring farming methods that cause minimal soil disturbance.

questions.question: Environmentally friendly farming practices have been profitable for Tom Watters.

analyses.content: 文中说 Tom 的这些措施非常昂贵（costly），而且并没有帮他获得更好的糖价，说明不仅没盈利，反而增加了成本。
(第6段) However, none of these costly initiatives has helped him get better cane prices.
